lessons.title: Less, But Better
lessons.key_idea: Instead of spreading your energy across many things, an Essentialist channels it into the few that matter most, making far more progress where it counts.

lessons.title: The Paradox of Success
lessons.key_idea: Success brings more options and requests, which can scatter our focus and quietly undermine the very clarity that made us successful.

lessons.title: You Can Have Anything, Not Everything
lessons.key_idea: Every yes is a no to something else, so instead of asking how to do it all, ask which trade-off you are willing to make.

lessons.title: Create Space to Think
lessons.key_idea: Discerning what is essential requires deliberately protecting time to think, rest, sleep and play, because a tired, crowded mind cannot see clearly.

lessons.title: If It's Not a Clear Yes
lessons.key_idea: Using extreme criteria, so that anything short of a clear yes becomes a no, frees you to commit fully to the best opportunities.

lessons.title: The Art of the Graceful No
lessons.key_idea: Saying no kindly but firmly, and cutting your losses on commitments that no longer fit, protects your time for what truly matters.

plan.title: Essentialism
plan.author: Greg McKeown
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's core framework, main chapters and key concepts well, though I would avoid citing finer details or exact wording from memory.
plan.one_liner: Stop trying to do everything. Learn to do only what truly matters, and do it brilliantly.
plan.summary: Greg McKeown argues that most of us are stretched thin, saying yes to too many things and making only small progress in a million directions. His answer is Essentialism: the disciplined pursuit of less, but better. An Essentialist accepts that we cannot have it all, so they deliberately choose the few things that matter most. The book is built around three stages. First, explore: create space to think, gather information and separate the vital few from the trivial many. Second, eliminate: cut the nonessentials, including learning to say no gracefully and walking away from commitments that no longer serve you. Third, execute: build systems, routines and buffers so that doing the essential things becomes almost effortless. The result is more clarity, more control and more meaningful contribution in work and in life.
